title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 199 (Recovery of remuneration in certain cases)

content.overview: Section 199 provides that without prejudice to any liability incurred under the Act or any other law, where a company is required to re-state its financial statements due to fraud or non-compliance with any requirement under the Act and the rules, the company shall recover from any past or present managing director or whole-time director or manager or Chief Executive Officer (by whatever name called) who, during the period for which the financial statements are required to be re-stated, received the remuneration (including stock option) in excess of what would have been payable to him as per restatement of financial statements.
content.glance: On restatement of financial statements for fraud or non-compliance: company recovers excess remuneration (including stock options) from past or present MD, WTD, manager or CEO for the restated period; statutory clawback, not discretionary.
content.study: Without prejudice to any liability incurred under this Act or any other law for the time being in force, where a company is required to re-state its financial statements due to fraud or non-compliance with any requirement under this Act and the rules made thereunder, the company shall recover from any past or present managing director or whole-time director or manager or Chief Executive Officer (by whatever name called) who, during the period for which the financial statements are required to be re-stated, received the remuneration (including stock option) in excess of what would have been payable to him as per restatement of financial statements. Current-law framing: confirm restatement triggered by fraud or non-compliance under the Act/rules; identify MD/WTD/manager/CEO who received remuneration in the restated period; compute excess over restated entitlement; company recovers that excess.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Company required to re-state financial statements due to fraud or non-compliance with the Act or rules.

sections.heading: Persons Covered
sections.body: Past or present managing director, whole-time director, manager, or Chief Executive Officer (by whatever name called).

sections.heading: Amount
sections.body: Remuneration (including stock option) received during the restated period in excess of what would have been payable on the restated figures.

sections.heading: Character
sections.body: Statutory recovery duty of the company; without prejudice to other liabilities under the Act or any other law.

provisions.title: Recovery of remuneration in certain cases

examples.title: Restatement after fraud
examples.body: Financial statements are restated after discovery of fraud that inflated profits. The MD’s commission for those years exceeds what the restated profits would have supported. Section 199 requires the company to recover the excess from the MD.

examples.title: Stock options included
examples.body: A whole-time director received stock options valued by reference to the original (inflated) results. On restatement, the excess value attributable to the restated period is within the recovery mandated by s. 199.

hypotheticals.question: Is recovery under s. 199 optional if the Board prefers not to pursue the former MD?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 199 states that the company shall recover the excess. It is a statutory duty, without prejudice to other liabilities, not a discretionary Board policy.

distinctions.title: Recovery on restatement (s. 199) vs excess under remuneration ceilings (s. 197)
distinctions.left: Clawback when statements are restated for fraud or non-compliance
distinctions.right: Refund of sums drawn above the s. 197 percentage ceilings

misconceptions.trap: Only current directors can be asked to return excess pay after restatement.
misconceptions.correction: Section 199 covers any past or present MD, WTD, manager or CEO who received excess remuneration during the period for which the statements are restated.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 199 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm restatement for fraud or non-compliance. II. Identify covered persons and period. III. Compute excess over restated entitlement. IV. Apply recovery duty. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Restatement facts; persons; excess computation; recovery claim; precise relief.

examTips: Trigger: restatement for fraud or non-compliance.
